source.title: Representations Shape Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Theoretical Insights and Empirical Predictions
source.authors: Yihao Xue; Ji-Ping Li; Baharan Mirzasoleiman

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes weak-to-strong fine-tuning theoretically and measures its outcomes in several empirical settings, but focuses on representation-based error predictions rather than Burns et al.'s PGR measure.
record.gate_note: The empirical sections report W2S error and its association with representation metrics, but do not give weak-supervisor and strong-ceiling comparisons sufficient to determine empirical PGR. Reported correlation values used to select hyperparameters are not recorded as W2S outcomes. The paper cites results from other work; those are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives theory (Thm 3.8, Thm 4.1, Example 4.2) on when a weakly supervised strong model improves on its supervisor. It tests empirically whether a label-free representation metric predicts W2S error across many weak supervisors (molecular tasks, ETHICS, and a Burns et al. NLP replication). The theory bears on V5; the predictor of W2S performance bears on V3. It reports no empirical weak-supervisor errors or PGR, so V1 is not tested empirically.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that W2SG is governed by the overlap between what the weak model's principal representations miss and what the strong model's principal representations cover. This explains which weak errors are replicated or benignly overfitted. The derived label-free metric predicts W2S error trends better than model size or dimension, including for fully fine-tuned LLMs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses weak-model labels to fine-tune stronger models and reproduces a Burns et al. NLP setup in one experiment, but its main contribution is a representation-based theory and prediction metric; it does not use or report Burns et al.'s PGR measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The association between the representation metric and W2S error varies with α and β hyperparameters, although the authors report positive correlations in most configurations. For end-to-end LLMs, results use a heuristic based on layer-wise activation maps.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267, 2025
record.problems: The main empirical results concern correlation between a representation metric and W2S error, not PGR or direct comparisons with weak-supervisor errors and strong ceilings across the tested models. End-to-end LLM representation extraction is acknowledged as heuristic. The text reports aggregate correlations, while individual scatter-plot values are not specified.
record.rows_left_out: Individual scatter-plot coordinates and additional dimension-comparison plots in Figure 11 were not recorded because their point values are not stated in the text and do not add a separately stated aggregate result beyond the dimension comparisons already included. Exact per-configuration heatmap correlations in Figures 6–7 were not individually transcribed; the paper's textual hyperparameter-sensitivity summary is recorded in r27.

untested.parts: No empirical weak-supervisor error, strong ceiling or PGR is reported for any real model pair; only the analytic toy example compares W2S with weak error.
No auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling or loss-variant comparison.
PGR itself (only Errw2s with a fixed strong model); variation with strong-model size; chess and reward modelling.
No exploitation, distribution-shift or error-similarity test.
Only sufficient conditions are given, not necessary conditions.
No vision or other non-language modality; the molecular tasks use transformers on SMILES.

missing.what: Figure 11: on SciQ, the metric gives SC=0.741 while dimension predictors give 0.272 and 0.428. On Amazon Polarity, the metric gives 0.786 while dimension predictors give 0.026 and −0.060 (smaller models). rows_left_out wrongly says no aggregate is stated.
Figure 5 left panel: the metric gives SC=0.905 on the Cosmos-QA subset with activation dimension ≤ 8000, the comparison set for r15–r16.

record.verdict_notes: The empirical measure throughout is Errw2s with a fixed strong model, not PGR; no weak-supervisor or strong-ceiling errors are reported for the real models. The toy example and theorems are analytic, so they were relinked from V1 to V5. Exp. III replicates the Burns et al. pipeline with Qwen-7B as the strong model and 28 weak LLMs. The paper is peer reviewed (ICML 2025).

versions.untested_parts: The toy example and a theorem under stated assumptions compare W2S performance with the weak model; the empirical model sweeps do not report PGR or direct weak-supervisor comparisons.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensemble, or loss-variant comparison is tested.
The paper studies representation metrics, model dimensions, and molecular and NLP tasks, but does not report PGR by model or task; it does not test chess or reward modelling.
No test of supervisor-uncheckable exploits, distribution shift, or error similarity between weak and strong models.
The paper gives sufficient conditions for improvement, not general necessary conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor.
No vision or other non-language modality experiment.
